cultivation.needs: Full sun and loose soil. Picked as the flowers open.
Any garden bed; it self-seeds happily.
Poor, dry soil suits it best.
Plant cloves in autumn; lift the bulbs when the leaves yellow.
A wet corner or a sunken, well-watered bed.
Acidic, waterlogged soil. A barrel of peat will do.
Thin, acidic soil and wind. Hates rich compost.
Any sunny bed. Cut leaves before it flowers.
Sown thick in spring and pulled whole, root and all.
A bramble patch along a fence. Mind the thorns.
A sheltered, sunny wall.
Warmth and very little water. It rots in cold, wet beds.
Damp straw and darkness. It thrives on neglect.
Shade, damp stone and still air. Grows on a north wall.
Loamy soil and morning dew. Harvest before midday.
A dry, sunny bed. Bundle and hang to dry.
Sown on disturbed ground. Sleepy bees are a good sign.
Grows among grass, feeding on its roots. Sow it into a lawn.
Cool, shaded soil. Gloves when handling; it is poison.
Deep-dug soil and plenty of manure.
Chalky shade. Keep it well away from anything edible.
A boggy, shaded bed. The bells ring faintly at dusk when ripe.
Needs real heat: a hotbed over a smithy or a brazier-warmed glasshouse.
Needs frost to ripen: an ice-packed cold frame or a winter bed.
Total darkness and rotting logs. Lights the cellar faintly blue.
Buried in dark, chalky soil around an old root.
Damp darkness. Those who sleep in the cellar have vivid dreams.
Needs absolute darkness. A single candle ruins the bed.
Constant damp: a dripping cellar or a covered well.
Grave soil in a sealed crypt or ossuary. The neighbours will talk.
Warm, humid glass and daily watering.
Pruned hard each week, or it takes over the glasshouse.
Must be tended by the same hands every day. It wilts when neglected.
Thin mountain grit and cold nights. Grown under glass in the lowlands.
A peat pool under glass, fed a dead insect or two each week.
Deep, rich soil. Pulling it screams: everyone within 30 ft who can hear makes a DC 13 Con save or is stunned for 1 minute. Stop your ears.
A dark, warm cellar on a bed of dung.
Absolute darkness and silence. Tenders hear whispering.
Damp stone ceilings. It grows upside down.
Under oak roots in a dark cellar. Gloves, always.
A fey grove or a warded circle. It edges away from careless tenders.
Planted in a true ring on a moonlit night. Stepping inside the ring is unwise.
Opens only under the full moon: harvest on that night or the bloom is lost.
A grove with a sleeping guardian. The tree fruits once each season.
A consecrated pool within the grove, kept clean by prayer.
Needs sunlight blessed by a cleric of a sun god at least once a week.
Any kitchen garden. The first thing every village healer plants.
A shaded, fenced corner, well away from the kitchen herbs and the children.
A sunny border. Bees will find it.

_note: Plants the party can grow in its own beds. site: plot | greenhouse | cellar | grove. Tending DC = the forage DC for that plant.
